elementary.citation: Excerpt adapted from a children’s nature article, 2024.
elementary.text: In the morning, the sun rises and gently warms the earth. Birds begin to sing, and small animals wake up to search for food. The sky slowly changes from dark blue to bright orange and yellow. Many children like to watch the sunrise because it makes them feel calm and happy.

questions.question: What happens when the sun rises in the morning?
choices: The sky becomes bright and colorful.
The birds go to sleep.
The animals hide underground.
The children go to bed.

questions.question: Why do many children like to watch the sunrise?
choices: It makes them feel calm and happy.
It is very loud and scary.
It helps them run faster.
It makes the night longer.

questions.question: Which animals are mentioned in the passage?
choices: Small animals and birds.
Whales and sharks.
Lions and tigers.
Only insects.

questions.question: How does the sky change during sunrise?
choices: From dark blue to bright orange and yellow.
From green to purple.
From white to black.
It does not change at all.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Sunrise is a peaceful time when nature wakes up.
Nighttime is the best time to play games.
Rainy days are always sad.
Children should stay indoors in the morning.

middle.citation: Excerpt adapted from a middle school science article on ecosystems, 2023.
middle.text: A forest ecosystem is made up of many living and nonliving parts that work together. Trees provide shade and shelter, while plants on the forest floor offer food for insects and small animals. Streams carry fresh water through the forest, supporting fish and other aquatic life. When one part of the ecosystem is harmed, such as when trees are cut down, the balance of the forest can be disrupted and many species may struggle to survive.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a forest ecosystem?
choices: It is a system where living and nonliving parts work together.
It is a place where only trees grow.
It is a habitat for humans only.
It is a system made only of water and rocks.

questions.question: What role do trees play in the forest ecosystem?
choices: They provide shade and shelter.
They remove all insects from the forest.
They stop streams from flowing.
They only serve as decoration.

questions.question: What might happen if many trees are cut down?
choices: The balance of the forest can be disrupted.
The forest will immediately grow more trees.
Nothing will change in the ecosystem.
Only the streams will be affected.

questions.question: Which detail from the passage supports the idea that different parts of the forest depend on each other?
choices: Streams carry fresh water that supports fish and aquatic life.
Trees are tall and green.
The forest can be visited by hikers.
The forest is sometimes quiet.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: A forest ecosystem is a balanced system where each part is important.
Forests are dangerous places that should be avoided.
Only animals are important in a forest.
Streams are the only useful part of a forest.

high.citation: Excerpt adapted from a high school article on digital citizenship, 2022.
high.text: In the modern world, digital citizenship refers to the responsible use of technology and participation in online communities. Students are expected to understand how their actions on social media, messaging platforms, and websites can affect both their own reputations and the well‑being of others. Practicing digital citizenship includes protecting personal information, respecting different viewpoints, and recognizing misinformation. When individuals think critically about what they share and consume online, they contribute to a healthier and more trustworthy digital environment.

questions.question: Which statement best defines digital citizenship as described in the passage?
choices: The responsible use of technology and participation in online communities.
The ability to vote using a computer.
Owning the latest smartphone and laptop.
Avoiding all social media platforms.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is it important for students to understand their actions online?
choices: Their actions can affect their reputations and the well‑being of others.
Their actions will always remain private.
Their actions only matter to close friends.
Their actions cannot be seen by anyone else.

questions.question: Which behavior is an example of practicing digital citizenship?
choices: Protecting personal information and respecting different viewpoints.
Sharing every rumor they read online.
Posting insulting comments about classmates.
Ignoring all privacy settings on social media.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about misinformation?
choices: Recognizing misinformation is part of responsible online behavior.
Misinformation is harmless and should be ignored.
Only experts can identify misinformation.
Misinformation is impossible to detect.

questions.question: Which sentence best states the central idea of the passage?
choices: Thinking critically about what we share and consume online helps create a healthier digital environment.
Technology should be used only for entertainment.
Online communities are always unsafe and untrustworthy.
Students should avoid participating in digital spaces.
